context.summary: Greenfield, time-boxed spike to validate the hypothesis that a JavaScript stack (Vue 3, PixiJS, Pinia, GSAP, the pathfinding package, and SQLite) can support an isometric, turn-based tactical RPG battle scenario similar to Final Fantasy Tactics (GBA), using the combat rules of Sistema Daemon, a Brazilian tabletop RPG created by Marcelo Del Debbio.
target_audience: The author (Pedro "Ratto" Paixão) and other RPG and tactics-game enthusiasts
key_use_cases: Configuring a battle (choosing player characters and enemies) and playing a full turn-based isometric combat to a win, loss, or draw condition
Using the finished prototype as a tangible demo to support conversations with potential partners

deployment_context.description: Brand new system (greenfield spike). No existing codebase or battle logic exists today beyond the default Vite + Vue 3 + TypeScript scaffold. Deployed as a static web app on Netlify (free tier), client-side only, no backend.

problems.description: No tangible proof of concept exists today for the Sistema Daemon tactical combat idea
problems.impact: Blocks investment and partnership decisions, since there is nothing tangible to show

problems.description: There is no concrete data on technical viability, development time, or cost for this kind of game with this stack
problems.impact: Makes any larger investment decision speculative, with high uncertainty on ROI estimation

goals.goal: Validate technical viability of the chosen stack
goals.metric: A full battle playable end to end without critical blockers

goals.goal: Quantify cost and time to estimate ROI for a larger project
goals.metric: Time and investment spent on development
goals.target: Recorded and consolidated at the end of the prototype

in_scope: Manual positioning of player characters within an 8x2 tile area; automatic random positioning of enemies across the map
Turn-based combat with different classes and terrain, following Sistema Daemon rules (detailed in the GDD)
Win/loss/draw condition when one or both sides lose all characters
out_of_scope: Character progression between matches (XP, leveling, items persistence)
Any screen beyond the initial configuration screen and the battle screen
Fine-tuned balancing of classes and terrain
Elaborate VFX/animation polish and a full music score
User authentication, personal data collection, and compliance requirements (no personal data is captured)
Accessibility support (screen reader, full keyboard navigation)

functional_requirements.name: Initial configuration screen
functional_requirements.description: The system must let the player configure a match before starting combat
main_flow: Player opens the prototype
Player selects the number and type of player characters
Player selects the number and type of enemies
Player confirms and starts the match
known_errors: Match cannot start with fewer than 3 or more than 6 player characters
Match cannot start with fewer than 1 or more than 6 enemies

functional_requirements.name: Initial positioning on the grid
functional_requirements.description: The system must let the player position their own characters before combat starts, and automatically position enemies
main_flow: Player manually places each of their characters within a fixed 8x2 tile area
System randomly places enemies across the map
alternative_flows: Player attempts to place a character outside the 8x2 area
Player attempts to place a character on an occupied tile or impassable terrain
known_errors: Invalid placement attempts are simply blocked by the system

functional_requirements.name: Turn-based combat loop
functional_requirements.description: The system must run combat as a sequence of turns ordered by initiative, letting each character move once and perform one action per turn
main_flow: At the start of each turn, initiative is rolled for each character as Agility + 1d10, minus any penalty carried from the action taken in the character's previous turn
Initiative penalties apply only to the next roll and do not accumulate
On a character's turn, the player (or AI) may move the character once, before or after acting
The character then performs one action: Attack, Cast Spell/Use Ability, Defend, or Use Item
known_errors: Attempting to move beyond the character's movement range
Attempting to attack a target out of range or without line of sight
Attempting to act with a defeated character
Attempting to act outside of the character's own turn
All of the above are blocked by the system with a developer-facing error notification (dev environment)

functional_requirements.name: Attack and damage resolution
functional_requirements.description: The system must resolve attacks using the official Sistema Daemon hit and damage formulas
main_flow: Hit chance is calculated as Active Source minus Passive Source plus 50
The attacking character rolls 1d100; the attack hits if the result is less than or equal to the hit chance
On a hit, total damage is calculated as damage dealt minus the target's Protection Index (IP)
Total damage is subtracted from the target's hit points
known_errors: Negative total damage must be clamped to zero and never heal the target
A character whose hit points reach zero or below is defeated and removed from combat
Attacking an already defeated target is blocked

functional_requirements.name: Movement and pathfinding
functional_requirements.description: The system must calculate and display valid movement tiles for a character's turn, respecting Movement and Jump attributes
main_flow: When it is a player character's turn, the system highlights all tiles reachable given the character's Movement (derived from Agility) and Jump attributes
Player selects a destination tile among the highlighted options
alternative_flows: Movement is a passive attribute indicating the maximum tiles a character can traverse per turn
Jump is a passive attribute indicating the maximum terrain height a character can climb or descend in one step; most characters have Jump 1

Each Jump used reduces remaining Movement by 1 (example: Jump 2 and Movement 6 spent 2 tiles horizontally plus a 2-tile height change in one step costs 2 Movement, leaving 2 more tiles of Movement available)
known_errors: Selecting a tile outside the highlighted reachable area is blocked
Selecting an occupied tile is blocked
Selecting a tile whose height change exceeds the character's Jump is blocked

functional_requirements.name: Simple enemy AI
functional_requirements.description: The system must control enemy characters automatically using simple decision rules
main_flow: On an enemy's turn, melee enemies move toward and attack the nearest player character
Ranged enemies try to keep a safe distance from player characters while staying within their own attack range
alternative_flows: No player character is reachable or attackable on the current turn
known_errors: If no attack is possible, the AI must choose to Defend or Use Item (if one is available) instead

functional_requirements.name: Combat VFX and audio feedback
functional_requirements.description: The system must play basic visual and audio feedback for combat events
main_flow: Every relevant combat event (attack, hit, damage, victory, defeat) triggers a simple animation (via GSAP) and a corresponding sound effect
alternative_flows: A required animation or audio asset is missing
known_errors: A missing asset must not block combat; it must only be skipped, with an error shown to the developer in the dev environment

functional_requirements.name: Victory, defeat, and draw condition
functional_requirements.description: The system must detect and resolve the end of combat
main_flow: After each turn, the system checks whether all characters on one side have been defeated
If one side has no characters left, combat ends and a simple victory or defeat message is shown
alternative_flows: Both sides lose all remaining characters as a result of the same turn
known_errors: This edge case must resolve to an explicit draw state, even though a draw is not expected to normally occur

specifications: Minimum of 30 FPS sustained during combat

Hypothesis: no custom uptime target; the prototype is a static site hosted on Netlify's free tier and relies on Netlify's standard SLA, as this is a low-stakes internal/partner demo rather than a production service
Hypothesis: no authentication or authorization required; the prototype is client-side only, publicly accessible via its Netlify link, with no sensitive user data

Structured console logging in the development environment for blocked actions (invalid moves, invalid attacks, out-of-turn actions) and missing assets; no external monitoring tool required for this prototype
Match state (unit stats, HP, positions, turn/phase data) lives only in memory (Pinia) for the duration of the browser session; there is no save/load and no session recovery
Static system data (Items, Weapons, Upgrades, Spells) is persisted in a read-only SQLite database, seeded at build time
Target the latest stable versions of Chrome, Firefox, and Edge on desktop; no mobile or legacy browser support
Not applicable: no personal data is captured by this prototype (hypothesis)
Not applicable for this prototype (hypothesis); no screen reader or full keyboard navigation support planned

architecture.approach: Client-side only single-page application built on the existing Vite + Vue 3 + TypeScript scaffold, deployed as a static site on Netlify. PixiJS owns the isometric canvas rendering (tiles, unit sprites, battle VFX) inside a composable tied to component lifecycle; Pinia holds all battle state as the single source of truth; composables contain pure combat logic (initiative, hit/damage resolution, movement/pathfinding rules) and call Pinia actions to commit results; the Vue + Tailwind HUD is a DOM overlay reading/writing the same Pinia store. Static system data (Items, Weapons, Upgrades, Spells) is served from a read-only SQLite database running in the browser, seeded at build time, as a deliberate proxy for the database integration the full product will eventually need.
components: PixiJS canvas renderer (tiles, sprites, VFX) owned by a usePixiApp-style composable
Combat composables (initiative, hit/damage resolution, movement/pathfinding rules using the pathfinding package)
GSAP for both canvas animations and HUD/DOM transitions
Tailwind-styled HUD (configuration screen, action panels, HP bars)
Read-only SQLite database (seeded at build time) for Items, Weapons, Upgrades, and Spells, queried client-side (e.g. via a WASM SQLite runtime)
Vitest for unit tests of critical combat formulas (initiative, hit chance, damage)
integrations: None external; the only "integration" is the client-side SQLite database used to validate the data-access approach intended for the future full product

decisions_tradeoffs.decision: Use PixiJS as the rendering engine
decisions_tradeoffs.justification: Canvas/WebGL renderer well suited to many animated sprites at once (tiles, units, VFX) for the isometric scene
decisions_tradeoffs.trade_off: Rejected Phaser (a full game framework with its own competing game loop) and DOM/SVG rendering (less suited to many animated sprites simultaneously)

decisions_tradeoffs.decision: Use the pathfinding npm package for grid traversal
decisions_tradeoffs.justification: Synchronous API and multiple algorithm options for A*, range, and distance queries on the isometric grid
decisions_tradeoffs.trade_off: Rejected easystarjs, which offers a similar feature set but with an asynchronous API; isometric screen-to-grid projection math is still hand-rolled rather than covered by any package

decisions_tradeoffs.decision: Use GSAP uniformly for all animation
decisions_tradeoffs.justification: A single API/timeline model for both Pixi canvas animations (movement, attacks) and HUD/DOM transitions (damage popups, panel transitions)
decisions_tradeoffs.trade_off: Avoids mixing Pixi's own ticker with CSS transitions, at the cost of depending on a single animation library for everything

decisions_tradeoffs.decision: Persist static game data (Items, Weapons, Upgrades, Spells) in SQLite instead of plain JSON
decisions_tradeoffs.justification: The intended full product will be integrated with a real database; this spike needs to prove that approach works end to end before committing to it at larger scale
decisions_tradeoffs.trade_off: Added client-side complexity (running SQLite, likely via WASM, in the browser) compared to the simplicity of a static JSON file, accepted because validating this integration is itself one of the spike's goals

dependencies.title: Game Design Document (GDD)
dependencies.description: At least a partial GDD detailing the Sistema Daemon combat rules (classes, terrain, formulas) must exist before or in parallel with development, as it is the source of truth for combat rules referenced throughout this PRD

dependencies.title: Static game data content
dependencies.description: The data for Items, Weapons, Upgrades, and Spells that will populate the SQLite database must be gathered and defined before that part of the system can be fully validated

dependencies.title: Visual and audio assets
dependencies.description: Character sprites, isometric tiles, and sound effects are not yet available. They will either be generated with AI tools or sourced from ready-made free or low-cost asset packs; visual quality is explicitly not a priority for this prototype, and audio/music can be deprioritized relative to the rest of the scope

risks.risk: Isometric pathfinding complexity (Movement/Jump rules) takes longer than estimated
risks.impact: Delays the prototype, affecting the time/cost measurement goal
mitigation: Implement a simplified version of pathfinding first (without Jump) and evolve it incrementally
Review the movement cost logic in isolation before integrating it with the UI
risks.contingency_plan: If the timeline becomes unsustainable, reduce the Jump rule to a single fixed value (e.g. always 1) and document the simplification as a deviation from the GDD

risks.risk: Runtime performance falls below 30 FPS on weaker machines
risks.impact: Poor experience when demoing the prototype to partners
mitigation: Limit the number of simultaneous sprites/effects
risks.contingency_plan: Reduce VFX quality or grid size if needed

risks.risk: SQLite-via-WASM integration brings unexpected complexity or compatibility issues
risks.impact: Delays the prototype and risks failing to validate this part of the architecture, one of the spike's explicit goals
mitigation: Validate the SQLite + WASM integration in isolation before populating all data
Keep a documented static JSON fallback ready in case WASM proves infeasible within the spike's timeline
risks.contingency_plan: If SQLite via WASM does not work in time, fall back to static JSON temporarily and record the limitation as a learning from the spike

acceptance_criteria: Player can configure a match by selecting between 3 and 6 player characters and between 1 and 6 enemies; outside these limits, the system blocks starting the match
Player can manually position their characters within the 8x2 tile area before combat starts
Enemies are automatically positioned randomly across the map when combat starts
Turn order is calculated by initiative (Agility + 1d10 minus the previous turn's penalty), with non-cumulative penalties
On each turn, a character can perform one move (respecting Movement and Jump) and one action (Attack, Spell/Ability, Defend, or Use Item)
Hit resolution follows the official Sistema Daemon formula (Active Source minus Passive Source plus 50, compared against 1d100)
Damage resolution follows the official formula (damage dealt minus Protection Index), never reducing hit points by a negative amount
Characters whose hit points reach zero or below are removed from combat
Enemy AI attacks the nearest player character when possible, keeps a safe distance when ranged, and uses Defend or Item when it cannot attack
Combat ends automatically when one side loses all characters, showing victory, defeat, or draw (when both sides are eliminated on the same turn)
Invalid actions (out-of-range movement, out-of-range/line-of-sight attacks, acting out of turn) are blocked by the system with an error shown in the dev environment
Basic VFX and audio trigger on combat events (attack, damage, victory/defeat); a missing asset does not block combat, it only logs an error in the dev environment
Static data for Items, Weapons, Upgrades, and Spells is queryable from the SQLite database seeded at build time
The prototype sustains a minimum of 30 FPS during combat on the latest stable versions of Chrome, Firefox, and Edge
The prototype is published and accessible via Netlify
Time and investment spent on developing the prototype are recorded by the end of the project

test_types: Unit tests (Vitest) for critical combat formulas: initiative roll, hit chance, and damage calculation
Manual/exploratory QA for the full combat flow, positioning, enemy AI, and VFX/audio feedback
testing_validation.strategy: Vitest unit tests isolate and verify the mathematical correctness of the Sistema Daemon formulas; manual QA by playing the prototype (npm run dev) validates the end-to-end battle experience, enemy AI behavior, and VFX/audio feedback, since there is no automated coverage for those areas
